articles.title: How to get Biggoron's Sword and Trading Quest Guide - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Guide - IGN
articles.summary: You can obtain Ocarina of Time's most powerful (and unbreakable) sword for Adult Link, the Biggoron's Sword, by completing a series of wacky trades
articles.body:
You can obtain Ocarina of Time's most powerful (and unbreakable) sword for Adult Link, the Biggoron's Sword , by completing a series of wacky trades all over Hyrule. You can start this epic side quest as soon as you have awakened as Adult Link, rescued Epona , obtained the Hookshot in Kakariko Village after becoming an adult (or Fairy Bow) , and unfrozen King Zora in Zora's Domain . Alternately, if you have not yet rescued Epona, you may still obtain the Biggoron's Sword once you have located the Longshot in the Water Temple , as the Longshot may also be used to cross into Gerudo Valley ( Note: Obtaining Epona is very helpful in terms of speed for the timed quests! Note that you cannot use songs to warp during these timed segments ). Finally, this guide is verified and is the same for Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, the GameCube collector's edition disc, the remake on Nintendo 3DS, and the Nintendo Online versions for Nintendo Switch and Switch 2.

Trade Quest Part 1: Biggoron Needs Eyedrops

Biggoron can be found at the top of Death Mountain (near the Great Fairy Fountain, to the right of the Death Mountain Crater entrance).

Talk to him and he will tell you that he is a master craftsman in need of help. He lost his ability to see and you must get eye drops for him so that he can continue making swords.

Trade Quest Part 2: Kakariko Village: Cucco Egg, Pocket Cucco, and Cojiro

Your next stop is Kakariko Village where you need to collect some rare Cuccos. In this case, the egg comes first, before the chicken. Err... Cucco.

During the daytime, talk to the Cucco lady (who gives you a Bottle for collecting all her Cuccos in a separate side quest) and accept her request to train a new, special type of Cucco. She will give you an unhatched Cucco Egg , called the Pocket Egg.

Go to a place where you can use the Sun's Song, like Hyrule Field. Use the Sun's Song to advance 24 hours to make the egg hatch.

Head to the house near the stairs (the ones leading up to the Potion Shop and the Bazaar) in Kakariko and use the Cucco to wake up Talon, who has been sleeping there since Ganondorf and Ingo chased him off. Now show the Pocket Cucco to the Cucco lady and she will give you a special Cucco: Cojiro , a blue Cucco that rarely crows.

Once you've obtained the Blue Cucco from the Cucco lady, head to the Lost Woods (you can warp to the Sacred Forest Meadow, if you know the Minuet of Forest ).

From the entrance to the Lost Woods, immediately turn left and locate the guy sitting on the ground. If you try to talk with him, he will ignore you. Show him Cojiro, and he will respond and tell you to give a Weird Mushroom to the lady that runs the secret Potion Shop in Kakariko.

However you have a strict two minute time-limit to do so. Run out to Hyrule Field, summon Epona and ride to Kakariko (do NOT use the Nocturne of Shadow to warp to the Graveyard, this will reset your quest). When you are not riding, try rolling as Link to move faster.

Trade Quest Part 4: The Return to Kakariko Village - Potion

Once you have made it to Kakariko, make sure it's daytime (play the Sun's Song if need be, it will not affect the timer).

Enter the regular Potion Shop and go through the passage to the left of the counter. Jump off the ledge, climb up the stairs and go through the door to enter the secret Potion Shop. Show the Weird Mushroom to the lady. In return, she will give you a Potion that will cure what ails the man in the Lost Woods.

Trade Quest Part 5: Back to the Lost Woods - Poacher's Saw

Return to the Lost Woods (you can warp there with the Minuet of Forest).

You will find that the man is no longer there. Instead you will find a cute little Kokiri girl. Show her the Potion, and she will insist that you give it to her. After you give her the Potion, she will give you the Poacher's Saw .

Trade Quest Part 6: Gerudo Valley - Broken Goron's Sword

Head to Gerudo Valley, which is located on the west side of Hyrule Field. This is where you need either Epona or the Longshot from the Water Temple to proceed.

Cross the bridge with Epona or the Longshot and give the Poacher's Saw to the master craftsman standing outside of the tent. He will give you the Broken Goron's Sword . You need to get it repaired by Biggoron.

Trade Quest Part 7: Death Mountain - Prescription

Head back east and climb to the top of Death Mountain once again, using the Fairy Bow or Hookshot to kill the Skulltulas on the face of the mountain (if you have learned it, you can use the Bolero of Fire to warp to Death Mountain Crater).

When you get to the summit, show Biggoron the Broken Biggoron's Sword. Unfortunately, he has a lot of ash in his eyes and needs you to help him before he can repair the sword. He will give you the eye drop Prescription and ask you to visit King Zora.

Trade Quest Part 8: Zora's Domain - Eyeball Frog

Head to Zora's Domain, and go up to King Zora's room. If he is still frozen, you will need to melt him with Blue Fire collected from the Ice Cavern , or bought from the Potion Shop at a high price.

In return, he will give you the Eyeball Frog . Be quick, as you only have three minutes before the frog is no longer usable. Hurry to Lake Hylia (do NOT warp with the Serenade of Water ).

Trade Quest Part 9: Lake Hylia - World's Finest Eyedrops

Once you enter Lake Hylia, head straight for the laboratory and enter it.

You will find a weird looking professor. Give him the Eyeball Frog, and he will make the World's Finest Eyedrops for poor Biggoron. You have four minutes to get the Eyedrops to Biggoron.

Trade Quest Part 10: The Race Against Time - Claim Check & Biggoron's Sword

Your goal now is to return to Death Mountain in under four minutes. The 4:00 timer is just barely enough to reach the summit using Epona, lots of rolling, and some tricks. If you fail, return to the lakeside lab and talk to the professor to try again. Remember, YOU CANNOT WARP. So don't try.

Race across Hyrule Field on Epona, go through Kakariko Village and up the ramps, rolling the whole way, and climb to the top of Death Mountain, avoiding as many enemies as possible and killing the Skulltulas on the final cliff with the Fairy Bow or Hookshot, once more. You cannot avoid these, you must kill them.

Give the Eyedrops to Biggoron. He will give you a Claim Check for the Biggoron's Sword. It takes three days and three nights for the sword to be repaired.

Use the Sun's Song six times so that three entire days pass. Show Biggoron the Claim Check to claim your prize: Biggoron's Sword . Biggoron's Sword does twice as much damage as the Master Sword. The only drawback is that you can't use your shield while Biggoron's Sword is drawn. It's a two-hander!

Also, the BIggoron Sword never breaks, unlike the Giant's Knife. Congratulations, you have finished this quest!

articles.body:
Disney Dreamlight Valley is a free-to-play life-simulation adventure game that features an extensive cast of characters consisting of heroes and villains from Disney and Pixar . Below, you will find a complete list of all characters that appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley, including all expansions and future characters that have been potentially teased.

Looking to learn more about a particular character in Disney Dreamlight Valley? Click the links below to jump to...

All Characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley

All Confirmed Disney Dreamlight Valley Characters

Characters can be spoken to daily in Disney Dreamlight Valley in order to complete Dreamlight Duties . In addition, you can also gift characters special daily gifts and even ask them to hang out, which will all increase their friendship level, and unlock unique rewards for each level you achieve.

While each character has a unique personality, friendship rewards, and gift preference, all of them can give you a hangout bonus, which you can choose when you reach a level 2 friendship with them.

Since the initial announcement trailer, Disney Dreamlight Valley has grown to include over 40 characters, each with a unique personality and questline. To learn more about each character, such as how to unlock them, all their related quests, gift guides, and friendship rewards, click the links in the table below to jump to our comprehensive character guides.

From Moana to Scrooge McDuck, here are all Disney characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Three characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley come from The Little Mermaid Universe.

Ursula is a powerful sea witch who likes to strike deals with people, but beware, her contracts might not be as good-hearted as they seem. With the release of the "Ursula's Transformation" Dream Bundle , she's back in her "Vanessa" disguise and up to her old tricks!

Ariel is the youngest daughter of King Triton. As such, she is one of the seven princesses of Atlantica.

This little mermaid has a never-ending curiosity for the human world, which leads her to strike a dangerous deal with Ursula, where she exchanges her beautiful voice to become human and get a pair of legs.

Eric is a dashing young man who also happens to be royalty. One day, while sailing, he was saved from drowning by a mysterious little mermaid.

He immediately fell in love with this girl, and, as they say, the rest is history.

Two characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley come from Moana's universe.

Moana is an energetic and optimistic lady who happens to be the daughter of the Chief of Motunui, which makes her an official Disney Princess. Moana cares a lot about her people and will do anything for them, including selling across the ocean to save them from a terrible fate.

Maui is a mighty demigod who has helped humanity numerous times, but he is as powerful as self-centered, so dealing with him can be exhausting. Nevertheless, he is an incredible addition to the Valley and can prove super helpful once you start doing quests for him.

For example, one of Maui's quest lead to you having coconuts grow at the beach, while another quest leads to you having a reinforced pickaxe that can destroy the blue-ish tropical rocks from the beach area.

In Disney Dreamlight Valley , Mickey and almost all his friends appear. These are the available characters in the game.

Mickey Mouse is a cheerful young mouse who would do anything for his friends. In Disney Dreamlight Valley, he loves to garden but is deeply saddened by the disappearance of his beloved Minnie.

Minnie Mouse is a sweet young mouse that is most known for being Mickey Mouse's long-time girlfriend.

Goofy is one of Mickey's best friends. He is always willing to help, but his clumsiness leads to more trouble. Goofy loves to fish, so you often find him near the ocean or a river trying to catch something.

Donald is another one of Mickey's closest friends. He means well but has a fiery temper that often makes him throw tantrums everywhere he goes.

Scrooge McDuck is Donald's uncle and a businessman at heart. He is always looking for ways to make a profit and take his many businesses to the next level. Whatever he does seems to pay off as he is one of the few ducks who can swim in money.

Daisy is Donald's girlfriend and one of Mickey's closest friends. She spent some time away studying The Forgetting but now is back in the valley ready to put her fashion sense to good use.

At the moment, there's only one character in Disney Dreamlight Valley that comes from The Sword in the Stone universe.

Merlin is one of the most powerful wizards you will ever encounter. Not only can he do magic, but he has the power to shapeshift, see into the future, cast enchantment, do alchemy, and many more things! As you can see, it's best to have this wizard as your friend, making him an incredible asset to the Valley.

Though Scar has been in the game already, since he was stuck in his home without the Forgetting affecting him, Nala and Simba join up later through unlocking The Lion King Realm. Then, you can make another journey back to the Realm to bring Timon and Pumbaa to the Valley.

Nala has been friends with Simba since they were cubs. Nala is nimble, fanatical, and capable. Simba is Nala's mate. Nala's quest line brings the Here and There Fish to the Valley.

Simba is the new leader of his kingdom and had to pass arduous trials. Simba is cheerful and adventurous, but anxious about his new role as a leader. Simba's quest line brings the Dreamlight Tree back to the Valley.

Scar is Simba's power-hungry uncle who wants to be King of Pride Rock. His arrival to Disney Dreamlight Valley unlocks the Vitalys Mines area for players to explore.

Timon is a meerkat and close friend of Simba's. He also comes from the Lion King Realm. When he moves to the Valley, he lives in Pride Rock alongside Simba and Nala.

Pumbaa the warthog is Simba's other best friend. He lives in the Lion King Realm at first and is brought to the Valley alongside Timon to spread some "hakuna matata" flair.

As one of Disney's most popular films, Frozen naturally has a lot of representation in Dreamlight Valley. Currently, there are four Frozen characters in the game:

We know about Kristoff's three things: he knows his way around the ice, his best friend in the whole world is a reindeer called Sven, and he loves Princess Anna with all his heart.

After her sister Elsa abdicated the throne to go to the enchanted forest, Anna became the Queen of Arandelle.

Unlike her sister, Anna often acts before she thinks, which makes her a fearless and caring person. She is always willing to help anyone in need, especially those he cares deeply about, like her future husband Kristoff, her sister, and Olaf.

Elsa spent most of her life scared of her icy powers. These feelings made her shut everyone out in fear of harming anyone around her. It wasn't until she fully came to terms with who she was that she was able to become who she was meant to be, the Fifth Spirit of the Enchanted Forest.

Olaf is the child-like snowman Elsa created. Olaf loves to give hugs, learn interesting new facts, and share his knowledge of anything and everything with anybody he interacts with. He is sincere, kind, naive, and cares deeply about his friends like Kristoff, Anna, and Elsa. Even though he is a snowman, he loves summer.

There are three characters from the Tangled universe that appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Mother Gothel wants to retain her youth at all costs and will go to any lengths to do so, even kidnapping baby Rapunzel from her crib to lock her up in a secret tower. While some of her actions aren't always morally right, she will be a valuable addition to the Valley.

Rapunzel, the spunky princess from Tangled, has been added to Disney Dreamlight Valley as part of the "A Rift in Time" expansion. She has been trapped in her tower on Eternity Isle by Mother Gothel but has managed to break free. You will meet Rapunzel while progressing through the expansion's main story, as she will help you find one of the Jewels of Time on Eternity Isle.

Flynn Rider is a charming and quick-witted thief most known for his appearance in Tangled. Flynn's love, Rapunzel, is not part of the Storybook Vale to begin with, but his quests follow Flynn as he works to make his way back to her.

Here are all Lilo & Stitch characters that appear in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Stitch is a prank-loving alien who crash landed in Dreamlight Valley. This little critter loves nothing more than spending time in the Valley with his ohana !

Only one character in Disney Dreamlight Valley comes from the Encanto universe.

Mirabel is from the Family Madrigal. She is optimistic, empathetic, and enthusiastic. Unlike many of her other family members, she does not possess a magical gift, but that does not stop Mirabel from finding her own ways to solve problems or tackle issues head-on. Some would say the epitome of " exceptionally unexceptional ."

Cinderella is one of Disney's most classic movies, and there are two characters from this film available in Dreamlight Valley:

The Fairy Godmother may be Cinderella's Fairy Godmother in the film, but in Disney Dreamlight Valley, she is everyone's Fairy Godmother! She is often forgetful to the point, where she may lose her wand; but she is boisterous, helpful, and always ready to grant people's wishes with her magic.

Cinderella has finally arrived in Dreamlight Valley as part of The Winter Ball Update . This iconic princess has long been a staple in the Disney universe, and during her storyline in Disney Dreamlight Valley, you'll help her recover missing tools from new animal friends, create an outfit that's fit for a ball, and much more.

Two characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley come from the gamified Wreck-it Ralph universe.

Hailing from the Wreck-It Ralph universe, everyone's favorite racing princess, Vanellope von Schweetz, glitches her way into the Valley and needs your help with navigating the brand-new feature, DreamSnaps . Upon helping, the prolific racer will join your Valley as a permanent resident.

As of the Pixel Perfect update in Disney Dreamlight Valley, Wreck-it Ralph himself smashes his way into the Valley! This gamified Villager starts out trapped inside a glitchy arcade machine, and you need to team up with The Forgotten to rescue him and unlock him in your Valley !

Five characters from the classic film Beauty and the Beast are currently available in Dreamlight Valley:

The heroine of Beauty and the Beast, Belle loves to read and has a sense of adventure. In Dreamlight Valley, she works as a librarian and helps Merlin maintain the Dreamlight Library .

The Beast may look imposing, but he's actually quite shy! He hopes to make plenty of new friends during his time in Dreamlight Valley.

Despite his (un)healthy obsession with Eggs and determination to marry the village's most beautiful resident, Belle, Gaston has taken up residence in Eternity Isle and needs help fixing his house and restoring his Meat Stall.

Lumiere loves to serve as the charismatic candlestick in the Beast's Castle. In Dreamlight Valley, he hopes to find a new role doing what he enjoys, all while solving a spooky mystery!

Cogsworth takes his job as Beast's majordomo seriously, so needs a little help finding his place in Dreamlight Valley. However, he soon finds purpose with helping Anna and running for Valley Mayor!

There are currently three characters from The Nightmare Before Christmas universe.

Everyone's favorite character, Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King from The Nightmare Before Christmas, joins Dreamlight Valley and, as you might suspect, can be found spreading his traditional holiday cheer to all of the Villagers!

Sally is a lovely rag doll from Halloween Town, as well as the girlfriend of Jack Skellington. In Dreamlight Valley she can be found maintaining her garden, working on various sewing projects, and spreading Halloween spirit alongside Jack!

Oogie Boogie is a scheming trickster who sows chaos in Halloween Town. He is unlocked as a Villager through a series of Quests in which you enter his Mirror Lair and play his twisted games, ultimately freeing him from the dimension where he has been trapped!

There are currently three characters from the Aladdin universe in DDLV.

The charming and slick Royal Vizier of Agrabah, Jafar, has arrived in Eternity Isle and needs your help freeing him from his temple, but not before causing a little trouble.

A clever street rat whose life was changed by a genie's lamp, Aladdin comes to Dreamlight Valley from the Agrabah Realm!

The princess of Agrabah, Jasmine's favorite things include keeping her city safe, researching magic, and spending time with Aladdin!

Currently, one Disney Dreamlight Valley character hails from Disney's classic shorts about Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: the titular rabbit himself.

Brimming with cartoon mischief, the cheeky, creative Oswald was stuck in the Sunken Ruins before being freed by the player. He's exclusive to the "A Rift in Time" paid expansion.

There are two characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley who come from the hit 1998 film Mulan:

The heroic Mulan disguises herself as a man to join the army and bring honor to her family - along the way, she saves all of China! In Dreamlight Valley, she runs a Tea Stall and keeps up with her training.

Mushu is the Guardian Dragon assigned to protect the Fa Family. Despite his small size, Mushu has a heart as big as China and is eager to keep Mulan safe and help her in all of her endeavors!

There is one character in Disney Dreamlight Valley that comes from the film the Princess and the Frog:

Tiana is a hardworking waitress who has always dreamed of opening her own restaurant. Through an unexpected adventure with Prince Naveen, she learns that dreams can grow and change. In Disney Dreamlight Valley, she runs her own restaurant, Tiana's Palace.

There are four character in Disney Dreamlight Valley that comes from the film Hercules:

Hades is the classic villain from Hercules. He has gray skin and bluish flame for hair. When wound up, however, this blue flame can burn red.

Hercules is the son of Zeus and is best known for his superhuman strength and kind heart. He joins the Valley with Phil, his well-known trainer, by his side.

Philoctetes, or Phil for short, is a Satyr known for training the legendary hero, Hercules. Despite his sometimes grumpy and rude demeanor, Phil has a big heart and is Hercules biggest ally.

There are currently two characters from Alice in Wonderland in Disney Dreamlight Valley:

Alice is a curious young lass who has magical adventures in Wonderland. She loves reading, learning new things, adorable animals, and hosting parties!

The Cheshire Cat is a clever, riddle-loving feline who hails from Wonderland. He has lots of mischief that he wants to make in the Valley before you can unlock him as a Villager.

There are currently four characters from Peter Pan in Disney Dreamlight Valley:

Peter Pan is the leader of the Lost Boys. He comes from Neverland and has found himself stuck inside Skull Rock until you can free him!

Tinker Bell is a character Disney Dreamlight Valley's Wishblossom Ranch expansion and is Peter Pan's loyal fairy friend. Tinker Bell needs your help with the Wishblossom Mountains' Pixie Dust problem to restore the Ranch to its former glory.

There are currently two characters from Sleeping Beauty in Disney Dreamlight Valley, both part of the Storybook Vale expansion

Maleficent is the Mistress of All Evil and a powerful magic wielder who feuds with Hades in the Storybook Vale.

Aurora is the titular princess from Sleeping Beauty. She goes missing in the Storybook Vale, but you can find her and bring her back as a Villager!

There is currently one character from the 101 Dalmations franchise in the Wishblossom Ranch expansion:

Cruella crashes her car in Glamour Gulch and needs your help to free it before eventually becoming an official Ranch resident!

Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs Characters

There is currently one character from the Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs franchise in the Wishblossom Ranch expansion:

Snow White is a classic Disney Princess who acts as the caretaker of Wishblossom Ranch in Disney Dreamlight Valley . She is close friends with all of the horses who reside there, and is dedicated to helping you stop the Decay and recover them all.

There are four characters from the Winnie-The-Pooh universe in Disney Dreamlight Valley:

Tigger is a bouncy resident of the Hundred Acre Wood and a friend of Winnie-the-Pooh. During the Wishblossom Ranch expansion, Tigger finds himself in a bit of predicament thanks to all the wish magic running amok in the Wishblossom Mountains!

Winnie the Pooh makes his grand debut in Dreamlight Valley as part of the Honeyglow Woods expansion . You'll find Pooh in the Drowsybloom Acre , where he'll need your assistance to restore his home, track down some misplaced honey, and reunite him with his missing pals.

Eeyore , Winnie the Pooh's gloomy friend, is the second character you will meet in the Honeyglow Woods expansion . As you progress through the main story, you'll eventually find Eeyore in the Gloommeadow , where he'll need your assistance to locate his missing tail, scare away the red monster, and restore his home.

Piglet is Winnie the Pooh's closest friend is unlocked during the Honeyglow Woods expansion , where he has gotten himself into quite the pickle. After your meeting, Piglet will ask for your assistance in freeing him from his home and conquering some of his most frightening fears.

There are currently two characters from Lady and the Tramp in Disney Dreamlight Valley. They are:

Lady is a lovely dog who lives with her owners Jim Dear and Darling. In Dreamlight Valley, she helps you deal with the strange magical spaghetti storm!

Tramp is a pup with street smarts who has started a new life together with his love, Lady. In Dreamlight Valley, Tramp is eager to make friends and go on lots of adventures with you!

There is currently one character from Disney's 'Pocahontas' in Dreamlight Valley, as Meeko is a Notable Companion rather than an official Villager:

Pocahontas is a kind and free-spirited character who has a special connection with nature. In Dreamlight Valley, Pocahontas is eager to prepare for the Celestial Celebration and Moontide Glow, as well as find her Raccoon friend, Meeko!

While most of the characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley come from existing films, there is currently one exception.

The Forgotten is a former ruler of Dreamlight Valley who was corrupted by the darkness. However, by completing the right Quests, you can welcome them back to the Valley.

From Buzz Lightyear to Wall-E, here are all Pixar characters in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Two characters from Pixar's Toy Story franchise have made their way to Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Buzz Lightyear is a proud Space Ranger who helps protect the Valley from a variety of dangers. He's also in charge of rounding up the missing alien toys around the Valley.

Woody is the bravest Sheriff in the West, and now he's here to bring his usual rootin', tootin' brand of fun to Disney Dreamlight Valley!

There are two characters from the Wall-E universe.

Wall-E is a friendly robot whose only job is to make his planet cleaner and greener so humans can return home one day.

EVE is an adorable little robot who lives on Eternity Isle, where she spends her time patrolling and keeping the island safe from danger. She also protects one of the most powerful Royal Tools in Disney Dreamlight Valley: the Royal Hourglass.

Only one character in Disney Dreamlight Valley comes from the Ratatouille universe.

Remy is a rat from Paris with big dreams and an incredible talent for cooking. Don't let his size fool you; this little guy can create the most fantastic dishes in all of Paris.

Currently, two characters come from the city of Monstropolis in Pixar's films Monsters, Inc. and Monsters University:

Mike Wazowski was formerly Sulley's Scarer assistant and is now a record holding Jokester at Monsters, Inc. He loves to play pranks, tell jokes, and let out enormous burps using his signature Green Soda !

James P. Sullivan, known as "Sulley to his friends, was once the most famous Scarer at Monsters, Inc. When the company switched over to laugh power, he took over as CEO. Sulley is hardworking and kind, but he still misses his friend Boo, who had to go back to the human world.

There is one character in Disney Dreamlight Valley who comes from the 2012 film, Brave:

Merida is the independent heroine from Brave. She is a strong character with red, curly hair as big as her spirit. Her favorite activities are archery and hanging out with her beloved horse, Angus.

Two emotions from the film Inside Out have made their way to Disney Dreamlight Valley:

Joy is always cheerful, which makes sense because she is the embodiment of Riley's joyful feelings. In Dreamlight Valley, she keeps things cheerful from her Remote Headquarters!

Sadness is an important emotion who helps Riley express those times when she is feeling unhappy. She joins the Valley alongside her friend Joy, where she lives at Remote Headquarters!

Although these characters did not make an appearance in the official trailer announcement, certain locations shown and other in-game hints have led us to believe we'll likely see some of the following characters:

More Underwater Characters (Little Mermaid, Finding Nemo, and more?)

articles.title: Critters Guide: How to Feed Animals and All Favorite Foods - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Critters are small animals that roam freely through the different locations and realms in Disney Dreamlight Valley. This DDV Critter guide details everything
articles.body:
Critters are small animals that roam freely through the different locations and realms in Disney Dreamlight Valley . This DDV Critter guide details everything you need to know about all 18 Critter types found across Dreamlight Valley , Eternity Isle , Storybook Vale , Wishblossom Ranch , and Honeyglow Woods , including where to locate each critter and their color variant, favorite food, and daily schedules .

Are you looking to learn more about a particular critter in Dreamlight Valley? Click the links below to jump to...

When approaching critters in Dreamlight Valley, you'll have the opportunity to feed them snacks in exchange for Dream Shards (when feeding them their favorite food) and the ability to unlock companions , which are essentially the closest thing to owning your own pet that will follow you as you explore the different locations and realms that the game has to offer.

As you might expect, not every critter is eager for human contact, so to feed every animal, you'll need to plan your approaches strategically , especially since only two variants of each critter will spawn in each location every day. Each critter needs to be approached differently , with how to approach them detailed below.

In addition, every critter in Dreamlight Valley also has their own favorite food that they prefer. When feeding animals these items -- which are found within their respective biomes -- you'll not only complete Foraging Tasks that'll earn you Dreamlight or Mist, but you'll also receive additional rewards in the form of Dream Shards, Motifs, or even Memories.

Obtaining a companion is fairly straightforward, as all you need to do is feed the same critter variant - any food will do - for a set number of days . While two is a common occurrence, the amount can vary depending on Critter. After feeding a particular critter variant for its set number of days , they'll become unlocked via your Collection log . Once unlocked, visit the Wardrobe menu and select Companion . Here, you'll find all the critters available to follow you around.

Every critter companion has five tiers of friendship levels that you can unlock. Each level brings with it a brand-new ability, which ranges from resource gifts, increased inventory space, the ability to gather more than one type of resource, and a chance to receive a random or unique piece of furniture, depending on the Companion type.

Dreamlight Valley Critters - All Favorite Foods and Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available in Dreamlight Valley, which is the village found in the base version of Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Eternity Isle Critters - All Favorite Foods and Color Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available to be found on Eternity Isle, which is part of the A Rift in Time expansion .

Storybook Vale Critters - All Favorite Foods and Color Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available to be found in Storybook Vale, which is part of the Storybook Vale Expansion .

Wishblossom Ranch Critters - All Favorite Foods and Color Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available in the Wishblossom Ranch Expansion .

Honeyglow Woods Critters - All Favorite Foods and Color Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available in the Honeyglow Woods Expansion .

Once you've managed to successfully approach a Hedgehog, you'll have the option to feed them.

How to Feed Squirrels Their Favorite Food

Found roaming the Plaza, Squirrels are among some of the friendliest critters you'll encounter in Dreamlight Valley. Easily approachable, Squirrels will not run away from you when approached unless they have already been fed within the last 24 hours .

Rabbits are much more skittish and will continually flee from you when initially approached. However, don't let their antics deter you; and instead, chase them down . As the saying goes, the third time's the charm, as on the third attempt , they'll finally settle down and allow you to interact with them.

If you're looking to complete the " Feed Rabbits Their Favorite Food " task , you'll want to feed them Carrots. Carrots can be purchased from Goofy's stall in Peaceful Meadow or simply grown from seeds you'll receive from removing Night Thorns throughout the Plaza .

How to Feed Sea Turtles Their Favorite Food

Often found swimming along the water's edge at Dazzle Beach, Sea Turtles are especially shy critters that will hide inside their shells when approached. However, when receding into their shell, wait a few moments, and they'll soon emerge, allowing you the opportunity to feed them.

A Sea Turtle's favorite food is Seaweed , which can be found along the shores of Dazzle Beach or beside any water source .

Like Rabbits, Foxes will initially run away from you when first approached. As a result, you'll need to chase these cheeky critters a few times until they eventually stop and allow you to approach them.

Foxes prefer fish as one of their ideal snacks, with the White Sturgeon Fish being their favorite. White Sturgeon can often be fished from the orange/gold fishing spots that appear in Frosted Heights .

How to Feed Raccoons Their Favorite Food

Raccoons are skittish critters that will flee from you when approached too quickly. To approach Raccoons correctly, you'll want to only move toward them when they are looking down. They'll quickly scurry away if you move while they are alerted, which is indicated by having their head in the air. Approaching Raccoons isn't easy, so don't be deterred if it takes several attempts before you're successful.

Blueberries are Raccoon's favorite food and can be found on bushes within the Forest of Valor or along Dazzle Beach .

You'll first need to clear the main bridge of tree stumps to reach the Raccoons that roam that Forest of Valor. This can only be done after receiving the Shovel Blade upgrade, which is obtained during the Welcoming Anna Quest that is unlocked via the Frozen Realm.

How to Feed Crocodiles Their Favorite Food

Much like Raccoons, Crocodiles are timid critters that will flee should you approach them too quickly. The key to approaching Crocodiles is to only move towards them when they are looking down. They'll quickly scurry away if you move while they are alerted with their head in the air.

Lobster is the favorite food of Crocodiles, which can be caught when fishing from golden fishing spots in the Glade of Trust.

How to Feed Sunbirds Their Favorite Food

Favorite Food : When it comes to feeding Sundbird's, their favorite food will depend on their wing color. So, here are the favorite foods for all Sunbird variants. Emerald Sunbird: Any Green or Yellow Flowers Golden Sunbird: Any Orange or Yellow Flowers Orchid Sunbird: Any Pink or Purple Flowers Red Sunbird: Any Red or Purple Flowers Turquoise Sunbird: Any Pink or Green Flowers

Emerald Sunbird: Any Green or Yellow Flowers

Golden Sunbird: Any Orange or Yellow Flowers

Orchid Sunbird: Any Pink or Purple Flowers

Turquoise Sunbird: Any Pink or Green Flowers

Despite their quick speed, Sunbirds are surprisingly friendly critters, so if they haven't already approached you first, chase after them, and they'll eventually stop, allowing you to approach them.

If you need help locating particular flowers types and colors, see our comprehensive guide for more:

Ravens favorite food in Disney Dreamlight Valley is any 5-star Meal . It’s a bit of a pricey requirement to please the Critters but it seems to be the only food that they favor. We fed them Bouillabaisse, Ranch Salad, and Ratatouille, all of which yielded the same result.

Ravens have five different color variations: Blue, Brown, Classic (Black), Red, and White.

When you feed a Raven a 5-star Meal, it will drop a Motif Bag as a reward. This will grant you a random Motif, which are decals that can be used when customizing clothing . If you’re a Disney Dreamlight Valley fashion aficionado, farming Ravens is a solid way to build up your inventory of Motifs.

Location Found : Depending on their color variant, monkeys can be found in The Ruins, The Courtyard, The Docks, and The Overlook.

Favorite Food : Banana Split - 5 Star Meal

Companion Unlock Time: You will need to feed Monkeys for three days in order to unlock them as a companion. The Toon Monkey takes four days.

To approach a Monkey, you must first participate in a game of tag, which will require you to chase after the Monkey several times until it eventually stops and allows you to approach it.

Once a Monkey allows you to approach, you'll have the chance to feed it. Now, while Monkeys will like any 3-star meal or above, their favorite food is the 5-star meal , Banana Split . To unlock a Monkey as a companion, you will need to feed them twice a day, across the span of three days .

When feeding a Monkey its favorite food, there's also a small chance you'll be rewarded with a Memory or Motif reward bag.

To make a Banana Split , you'll need 1 Slush Ice , 1 Banana , 1 Milk , 1 Sugarcane , and 1 Sweet .

Lastly, Monkeys also come in six color variants , which are all found in various locations around Eternity Isle. These colors include Beige, Black and Brown, Black and Gray, Classic Gray, Red and Beige. After completing the Quest " The Spark of Imagination ," the Toon Monkey will also appear.

Location Found : Depending on their color variant, Cobras can be found in The Wastes, The Plains, The Borderlands, The Oasis, and The Borderlands.

Favorite Food : Eggs - Purchased from Remy's Restaurant.

Companion Unlock Time: You will need to feed Cobras for four days in order to unlock them as a companion.

Much like Racoons, you'll need to approach Cobras cautiously , as their skittish nature can make them hard to approach them. The key to approaching a Cobra is only to move while its head is down , as each step towards them will cause them to raise their heads in the air. If you move while their head is raised , they'll quickly bolt away , and you'll need to restart the process.

Once you're close enough to a Cobra, you will have the option to feed them. But just be careful not to move . Otherwise, you'll need to regain their trust all over again.

While Cobras will like food items such as Scorpions , their favorite food is Eggs , which is a cheap ingredient that can be purchased from Remy's Restaurant . When feeding a Cobra its favorite food, there's also a small chance you'll be rewarded with a Motif.

Lastly, Cobras come in six color variants , which can be found in various locations around Eternity Isle. These colors include Blue and Red Striped, Classic Purple and Red Striped, Green and White Striped, Pink Spotted, and Yellow and Purple Striped. After completing the Quest " The Spark of Imagination ," you will also unlock the Toon Cobra.

How to Feed Capybaras Their Favorite Food

Location Found : Depending on their color variant, Capybaras can be found in The Promenade, The Grove, The Grasslands, and The Lagoon.

Favorite Food : Cabbage - Purchased from Goofy's Stall in The Grasslands, The Promenade, The Grove, and The Lagoon

Companion Unlock Time: You will need to feed Capybaras for three days in order to unlock them as a companion. The Toon Capybara takes four days.

Unlike other critters , such as Monkeys and Cobras , Capybaras are friendly little creatures that can be approached without any adverse reactions. So, simply approaching a Capybara in any form will allow you the opportunity to feed them.

While Capybaras will like food items such as Yams , their favorite food is actually Cabbages , which is a vegetable that can be purchased at Goofy's Stalls in The Grasslands, The Promenade, The Grove, and The Lagoon. When buying Cabbage Seeds , it's important to note that they take one in-game hour to grow and will only yield one Cabbage per plant .

When feeding a Capybara its favorite food, there's also a small chance you'll be rewarded with a Motif.

Lastly, Capybaras come in six color variants , which can be found in various locations around Eternity Isle. These colors include Black and White, Blue Striped, Classic Brown, Gray Spotted, and Red and White. After completing the Quest " The Spark of Imagination ," the Toon Capybara will also be an option to befriend and feed.

Location Found: Storybook Vale: The Bind

Companion Unlock Time: Brown and Purple Owls take two days to tame. Light and Dark Owls, however, take four days of feeding to tame.

Owls are friendly critters, so they are happy for you to approach them as normal. Once you approach an Owl, interact with it to feed it and select Barley or any other type of Grain. Barley is the Owl's favorite food , but they also like any kind of Grain ingredients.

If you feed an Owl Barley, you have a chance of receiving 2x Pine Cones, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard as a bonus reward. If you feed an Owl any other type of Grain, you have a chance of receiving a Decal, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard.

Location Found: Storybook Vale: Mythopia

Companion Unlock Time: Pink, Blue, Black, and Yellow Pegasi can be tamed in three days. Peach Pegasi, however, need to be fed for four days.

Pegasi only live in the Mythopia region of the Storybook Vale, which means you will need to collect 2000 Story Magic to make it to the Elysian Fields at least. Once there, you will have to track down a Pegasus.

Pegasus are small creatures that are absolutely bursting with energy, meaning you will have to tire them out before you can approach and feed them. They follow a similar pattern to other energetic Critters in the game, like Rabbits, for example. So, if you've had experience tracking down a Rabbit, you will know exactly what to expect. Stay on their tail, and they will tire themselves out eventually.

Once you approach a Pegasus, interact with it to feed it and select a Vegetable Meal, preferably a 4+ Star one. Four Star Vegetable Meals and above are the Pegasus's favorite food , but they like any kind of Vegetable Meal.

If you feed a Pegasus its favorite food, you have a chance of receiving 2x Lightnings, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard as a bonus reward. If you feed a Pegasus a 3 or lower Star Vegetable Meal, you have a chance of receiving a Decal, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard.

Companion Unlock Time: Blue, Red, Green, and Teal Baby Dragons can be tamed after feeding them for three days. Purple Dragons, however, need to be fed for four days.

Dragons can only be found in the Everafter region of the Storybook Vale. That is one of the two regions locked behind a tall, gnarly gate of Ink. You will have to collect at least 200 Story Magic to unlock the way to the Wild Woods.

Baby Dragons are friendly critters for the most part, but they are a little shy at first. That means you will have to approach them slowly and with caution so as not to spook them. When they are anxious, they will be tightly curled up on themselves. Wait until they have relaxed before proceeding closer.

Once you approach a Baby Dragon, interact with it to feed it and select Magma , Pure Ice , or any type of Gem . Magma and Pure Ice are the Baby Dragon's favorite foods , but they will be happy with any kind of Gem.

If you feed a Baby Dragon its favorite food, you have a chance of receiving 2x Petrified Wood, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard as a bonus reward. If you feed a Baby Dragon a Gem, you have a chance of receiving a Decal, a Dream Shard, or a Memory Shard.

Location Found: You can find different Geese color variations across the Wishing Alps region around its five areas: Wishblossom Ranch, Wishing Way, Delver Dale, Silver Summit, and the Ranch Highlands.

How to Approach : Similar to Squirrels , you don't need to approach Geese in any special way as they won't run away. You can simply approach Geese by walking or running up to them and interacting with them.

Liked Foods : Strawberry, Gooseberry, Raspberry , and Blueberry .

Geese are jolly, friendly creatures who you can find roaming the lands of Wishblossom Alps. Approach any Goose by walking up to it and pressing the 'Approach' option to interact with it by feeding its Favorite Food, Red Currants , which you can find growing on bushes in any area of Wishblossom Alps. Alternatively, you can feed them their Liked Foods , which are Strawberries, Gooseberries, Raspberries, or Blueberries . Geese will jump for joy on receiving their Favorite Food, making them a delight to feed.

Location Found: Different color variations of Skunks can be found across the Glamour Gulch region around its four areas: Paisley Park, Runway River, Modish Marsh, and Haute Plateau. You can unlock Glamour Gulch by raising your Friendship with Maximus to Level 3 during "The Decay of Fashion" Quest, enabling him to jump the gap across the bridge to reach it.

How to Approach : Similar to Raccoons , move cautiously and only when the Skunk has its tail lowered.

Liked Foods : Any Fruits , Any Vegetables , Egg , Cheese .

Skunks are small creatures with a lot of energy, so they will give you the runaround unless you approach them cautiously. If you chase them, they will keep running away. To prevent them from running, you will need to approach Skunks when they are standing still in a relaxed posture with their tails down. If you approach a Skunk while its tail is raised and alert, it will run away. As you get closer to a Skunk, it will curl up into a small ball, allowing you to interact with it by pressing 'Approach'.

Once you approach a Skunk, interact with it to feed its favorite food - either a Button Mushroom or a Pincushion Peach , which you can harvest around Glamour Gulch. You can find Button Mushrooms growing on the ground, and gather Pincushion Peaches from fruit trees. Skunks also like any Fruits , any Vegetables , Egg , and Cheese !

Location Found: Different color variations of Bees can be found throughout the Pixie Acres region . Pixie Acres is a region that you can unlock by raising your Friendship Level with Khan so that he can kick down the metal barrier leading to the region. The four areas inside Pixie Acres are Sundae Shores, Hundred Acre Fields, Pixie Flats, and Hunny Falls.

How to Approach : Like Rabbits and Pegasi , Sweet Bees must be chased before you can approach them. Simply chase after them 3-4 times to tire the Bee out. Once they have stopped moving, you can Approach and feed them.

Favorite Food: Honey Coral - Found by fishing in white ripples in all areas of Pixie Acres.

Bees have a lot of energy and will fly off if you approach them. You need to match their energy and continue to chase after them! Each time the Bee moves away, keep following it. Eventually, it will tire out and you will be allowed to approach. If you want to move faster while chasing a Bee, you can Sprint or Glide or Gallop on one of your horses .

Once you Approach a Sweet Bee, feed it a Honey Coral , which can be found by fishing in white ripples anywhere in Pixie Acres. If you don’t have any Honey Coral, they also like any and all types of Flower !

How to Feed Hedgehogs Their Favorite Food

Favorite Food: Pufflebud Pods or Golden Honey

To approach a Hedgehog, simply walk towards them and as they curl into a ball , stop and wait a moment for them to uncurl. Once they've uncurled , approach and interact with them .

When you've managed to successfully approach a Hedgehog, you'll have the option to feed them. Feeding them their favorite food , Pufflebud Pods or Golden Honey , three times will unlock them as a companion.

Golden Honey can be harvested from The Busy Bees' House , which you construct during Winnie's Chapter 1: All You Need Is Honey Quest . Pufflebud Pods can be harvested from seeds purchased at the restored Hunny Stall in Drowsybloom Acre. The stall can be repaired by picking up the Shopping List that's found on the ground, just in front of the stall.

Important Note: Due to the way feeding works, unlocking Hedgehogs as a companion will take three days of feeding favorite food once per day . You can keep track of feeds by looking for the food icon that appears in the button right corner when in the feeding menu. If it's ticked green, it means you've completed the favorite food feeding for the day.

The Keepsake Sea - All Favorite Foods and Color Variants

Below is a complete list of all critters and variants available in the Keepsake Sea expansion.

How to Feed Toucans Their Favorite Foods

Time To Unlock As Companion: One feeding

If you feed a Toucan its Liked foods, which are any Fruits , you'll receive a Dream Shard and a Memory Shard. If you feed a Toucan its Favorite food, Lychee , you'll recieve a Dream Shard, Memory Shard, and Motif Bag.

Toucans won't run when you approach when you're first feeding them, so no tricks necessary to hand 'em some food. (You can only feed once in 24 hours, though.)

How to Feed Meringuins Their Favorite Foods

Companion Unlock Time: Two feedings If you feed a Meringuin its Liked foods, which are any Fish , you'll receive a Dream Shard and a Memory Shard. If you feed a Meringuin its Favorite food, Candy Pebbles , you'll recieve a Dream Shard, Memory Shard, and Motif Bag.

Meringuins are playful and like to be chased, so you must chase them down three times. At the third try, they'll let you approach to feed them.

How to Feed Axolotls Their Favorite Foods

Time To Unlock As Companion: Three feedings If you feed an Axoltotl its Liked foods, which is any Seafood , you'll receive a Dream Shard and a Memory Shard. If you feed an Axoltotl its Favorite food, Pink Coral , you'll recieve a Dream Shard, Memory Shard, and Motif Bag.

Axololts are timid and should be approached slowly. If they go into hiding, don't give up. Be patient and they'll emerge again for you to try to approach.

Note: This information was provided by the developer and has not yet been tested.

articles.title: Fire Temple Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. With the Goron people kidnapped, it will be up to Link to brave the fiery temple and rescue the imprisoned Gorons, while seeking out the new sage within the heart of Death Mountain.

Equipped with a new Goron Tunic to survive the blistering heat, Link has learned a new melody to transport himself to the Fire Temple. You'll need to not only seek out the Fire Sage and the Medallion they hold, but also find a way to rescue all the imprisoned Gorons before they are sacrificed to a wicked dragon.

Entering the Fire Temple, you of course need to be prepared to deal with fiery threats. The Goron tunic is a must for surviving its more superheated rooms, and you'll need to be extremely cautious around anything that might threaten to take that tunic away.

The main entry hall has a few Fire Keese floating around four doors: One is locked, another is blocked by a large statue, and a third on the bottom left leads to an imprisoned Goron (and a very large chest) you can't rescue yet. You're only path forward seems to be taking the upper left path to the west.

It's here you'll find a large room leading to the boss, but someone has beaten you to it: Your sworn brother, Darunia! He'll ask that you help him out as he seeks to face the dragon Volvagia alone, and rescue his nine Goron brethren before the dragon can gobble them up. He'll promptly leave through the far door, and since it's too far to jump you'll have no choice to but to accept his wishes.

Luckily, you won't have far to go to start your quest of freeing the Goron people. From the door, head down to the south and hop across several platforms above the raging lava to reach a far ledge.

Here you'll find the first of nine imprisoned Gorons, and you can step on the switch to free him. He'll see himself off to Goron City on his own, but will give you a clue that maybe a pillar above can be dislodged to reach Darunia.

It's a fair start, and he'll also leave behind a small Treasure Chest with a Small Key! In fact, each Goron you rescue has a key of their own, making it doubly worth your while to play the hero!

Now that you have a small key, return to the entry hall, and cross to the east side to open the door into the large chamber beyond.

This large room is full of more raging lava, a long bridge spanning the cavern, and several moving platforms to the north and south. Fire Keese are everywhere, so be sure to snipe them from afar so you don't get ambushed in the middle of a jump across the lava.

First, turn your attention to the north, where the next Goron can be seen behind a cage. You can move across the large stone platforms to reach him, just beware that some will start to sink, so move quickly to the far side. Step on the switch to free the second Goron, who has another small Treasure Chest, and a hint - some of the walls have an odd texture that means they can be bombed!

Once he departs, claim the Small Key inside.

Stay along the north side of the room and move to the east, hopping across more sinking and moving lava platforms while watching out for Lava Bubbles that can hop out of the fires to attack -- shield them away then follow up with a Hookshot.

There's a high ledge in the northeast corner, and if you step on the platform in front of it, the platform will boost up into the air from a jet of lava below. Up here, there's another one of those strange blue blocks that you can play the Song of Time in front of to move it from its high position down below, letting you climb into a room beyond.

In here, you'll face off against several Flying Tiles -- floor tiles with a mind of their own. They aren't exceptionally difficult, as you just need to lock on and raise your shield to deflect as they smash into you.

The real problem is what's lurking behind them as it tries to get close while you're distracted: A Like Like. These icky looking slug things will try and get close enough to extend their body and swallow you whole. If they do, they can even steal items from you -- which include the likes of your Hylian Shield and Goron Tunic!

The good news is if you act quick and defeat them, they'll spit out the last thing they stole. Use the hookshot to stun their body and hit them with a strong attack, before backpedaling to avoid their reach and repeat.

After clearing out the room of Flying Tiles and the Like Like, be sure to inspect the back wall, and you'll find that the Like Like was guarding a Gold Skulltula you can defeat to claim its token!

Exiting the room with the Like Like, make your way to the opposite south side of the large chamber, hopping over moving platforms as you go, and remember the Goron's words about funny looking walls.

There's a cracked wall along the southern edge of the lava lake. Toss a bomb at it, and you'll reveal yet another imprisoned Goron.

Like the last one, he's also got a small Treasure Chest, and you can step on the switch to rescue him and get another hint: a room nearby has a platform that shoots upward with a huge pillar of flame. Sounds like a good way to get higher in this dungeon.

As you turn to leave, note the pair of platforms off in the lava along the southwest. The second platform will actually shoot up into the air, leading to a hidden ledge you can jump to with pots full of Blue and Red Rupees!

Finding the Fourth Goron and Dungeon Map

Make your way across the long bridge to the east side of the cavern room, and open the locked door to the next area. Just as the Goron said, there's a huge jet of fire coming from the center of the room, you'll just need something to put on top of it.

Head past the jet of fire to a second locked door to open it, and climb the mesh wall up to the top of the room. Be wary, as the walls here are lined with Keese lying in wait to ambush you if you try to go for the pots in the corners.

Push the large stone block on the edge over the flame jet, and then hop down to ride the makeshift elevator up to floor 2F!

The room up here is full of Torch Slugs, slow moving but aggressive slugs that leap at you when they're on fire. The good news is you can simply shoot them from afar, or dash into slice at them and extinguish their flames.

Head up the large steps to find a wall of flames blocking your path next to a strange blue switch. Hit the switch to turn it pink, and the fires will recede, appearing against the back mesh wall instead.

Look in a corner alcove for a stone block to pull out and use as a platform to climb up and move past where the first wall of fire was, then turn around hit hit the switch again with your Bow or Hookshot, changing where the fire walls emits from, and allowing you to climb up to floor 3F. There's a Goron prisoner nearby, but no switch to release him. Sorry guy, you'll have to wait a bit longer.

Up on the third floor's east side, you'll find a huge room full of rolling boulders moving through tight corridors with several platforms above them. Since you can't climb up to them, you'll need to navigate the lower roads carefully.

As soon as you enter the large area with rolling boulders, stick to the right wall and move north to spot a cracked wall. Toss a bomb over, and you'll uncover a Gold Skulltula here!

Stick to the northern walls past where the spider was, and dodge more boulders to spot an alcove with another imprisoned Goron. Step on the switch to release him, and he'll pass along the small Treasure Chest he was holding, along with a hint: some doors in the temple are fake, and will fall down on top of you unless you bomb them first.

After he leaves, claim your next Small Key.

Next, carefully weave along the rolling boulders to the south side of this large room, and you'll find another large alcove. This one doesn't have a prison gate, but it does have a large Treasure chest holding the Dungeon Map!

Finding the Fifth and Sixth Goron and Compass

The other prison in this room is up on the high platforms, so you'll have to leave it for later. Instead, look along the western side of the room for a locked door you can now open, and enter a connecting passage.

Inside here, there's a door to the south, and a sealed door with an eye target up to the west. Shoot the eye and take the western door first, leading to a small enclosed area overlooking the western part of this large area, and more importantly, a large Treasure Chest with the Compass!

Now, enter the southern door to enter the main part of the room -- a large lava pool with several mesh platforms. However, as soon as you start across, a wall of flame will begin coming up from behind.

Sprint up the walkway and dodge the Red Bubbles until you can spot a ledge on the left. Pull yourself up and wait for the wall of fire to pass you. The door here is locked, but you can still catch your breath before jumping back down and running behind the fire wall tto the northern side.

There's a large stone block here, and you can push it out back into the previous room, not only giving you a shortcut, but access to the high platforms over the rolling boulders.

Before moving back along these raised platforms, hop north and then look back south and upward, where you can spot a gust of straw. If you confirmed the Scarecrow's Song in Lake Hylia, you can play it here to summon Pierre up above.

Hookshot up to him, and then look for a small platform to the north to jump to, and it will automatically rise up, leading to a mesh wall up to the top floor. It's here you'll find a Gold Skulltula along the wall by the door.

In this top floor room, you'll find several small Treasure Chests with Rupees inside, but you can also look along the inside of the inner wall around the pit to find one more Gold Skulltula to hit with your Hookshot.

To reach the three chests, you'll need to step on a switch to raise two pillars with Hookshot targets, and then race along the room to hook each one before the descend. Your reward will be two Red Rupees and a Purple Rupee - 90 Rupees in total!

Head back down to the platforms above the previous room, and carefully leap over the rolling boulders. Take out the Fire Slugs as you make your way to a central platform with a large crack in it.

Toss a bomb over to the cracked platform, and it will explode to reveal a pit with a mesh wall. This leads back down to floor 2F where you first came up and passed the imprisoned Goron. On this side however, you'll be able to step on a switch to free him.

He'll also leave you with a small Treasure Chest and a clue: some switches are so rusted that even Gorons aren't heavy enough to budge them.

Climb back up to the high platforms, and continue leaping across the boulders below to reach the southern end of the room. Up here, you'll find one more prison gate that you can open by stepping on the switch, revealing your next Goron prisoner to free.

Like the others, he has a small Treasure Chest, and a new hint for you: The temple's hidden treasure is a big old hammer, which sounds like a fine addition to have!

Finding the Seventh Goron and Megaton Hammer

Now that you have two new small keys, make your way back to the large room with the fire wall that chased you along the mesh platforms. Sprint back to the eastern side ahead of the approaching fire wall to enter the next area.

In this next large room, you'll find a veritable fiery funhouse of hidden flame wall and flame spouts all designed to drive you insane. You'll want to step very cautiously through this area, or risk taking a lot of damage over time if you get frustrated.

Start by heading north around a moving flame jet and several rolling boulders moving back and forth. The thin posts between them can alight with hidden flame walls when you draw close, so try and carefully move around to spot an opening before planning your next move.

Speaking of funhouses, do not trust the door to the south of the first rolling boulder. If you watch it closely, it will wiggle from time to time, and if you try to open it, the door will just fall flat on your face and damage you. Toss a bomb at it instead to be done with the phony.

Instead, navigate through the first few hidden flamewalls to reach the northern wall where another Goron is imprisoned.

The switch to open his cell is right in front of him, and he has a small Treasure Chest for you along with a tip: If the way is blocked, the key to getting through is "time". Okay.

You'll find that from the Goron's prison, all the posts in the western direction will deny you with flame vents, meaning you can't cross to that side of the room from this direction, so head back to the south side of the room.

On this side, fun comes in the form of more fire spouts and hidden flame walls among the rolling boulders, as well as a few Fire Keese to harass you from above. Note that you can make your way to the far west in this area to find another fire spout guarding some pots with Hearts if you need them, otherwise, look for a locked door to enter the central chamber.

There are bars on both sides in here, meaning you can't reach the other Goron prisoner from this angle, so instead keep heading north to the side of the room you couldn't reach earlier.

There's still more hidden flame walls to navigate around with an added twist: A switch in the middle of this area needs something permanent to sit on it to unseal the large flame vents to the west. Ignore the fake door to the north, and carefully navigate a path east and north to a small platform with a tiny stone block, avoiding a rolling boulder and both a spinning and stationary flame spout as you go.

Once you reach the two stones, grab one, and toss it through the fires over toward where the switch is, so you don't have to worry about carrying it all the way back.

Return the way you came, and weave up by the large flame jets to the north wall, past the fake door and down to the switch, where you can now place it on the switch. Thankfully, this will not only stop the large flame jets, but all fire traps in the room! Hooray!

Entering the next room using your last key, you'll be locked into a small arena with a Flare Dancer, who jump out of a fiery pit in the middle and begins to skate around the room. It can emit large fiery spin attacks as it skates by, and won't take any damage in its current form.

Instead, ready your Hookshot and wait until it get close to yank its metal core out out from the fire. The tiny body will become vulnerable, and try to comically skedaddle away from you, which is your moment to start hacking away with your sword.

The little guy is pretty fast, and after a bit of punishment he can often outpace you. However, given how small the arena is, you can simply run the other direction to cut him off, or use the plentiful Bomb Flowers to toss in his way.

After taking enough damage, he'll replenish his flames in the fire pit in the center, while also expelling a few blue flames that will bounce around the room, giving you hazards to be mindful of and keep away from as you repeat the process of yanking him out of his fiery form. Keep this up, and he'll soon explode away, causing a platform to fall onto the pit and open up a lift to floor 4F.

Take the lift up to a connecting area to the top floor, and start climbing up. Similar to another connecting room, you'll find flame jets here blocking the path with a colored switch below. There are plentiful Bomb Flowers in this room as well, and you can toss one down to the switch to lower the jets, then toss a second Bomb Flower while you run toward the flame jets blocking the mesh wall to climb up after the detonation.

At the top of Floor 5F, you'll find a circular room with a rolling boulder blocking your path to the right, and a switch in front of you.

Step on it, and it will raise a very narrow path up to the top level where the flame walls will temporarily lower. Quickly run up the narrow path before the fires return. It's here you'll find the grand prize: The Megaton Hammer!

With this tool, you can not only deal damage by slamming down the hammer, but you'll also be able to break apart things like grey rocks, rusted switches, and large statues!

Be sure to leave along the high ledge along the south above the rolling boulder. At the far end of the high ledge, you can find some Fairy writing about loving bright places. Let the sun shine in with the Sun's Song, and the fairy magic will heal you!

To leave this area, look along the north for a large raised button over a grate, and use the Megaton Hammer to slam down, creating a hole to jump down.

You'll get a few more tutorials on using the Megaton Hammer as you drop down. A large segmented statue blocks the next door, but you can swing your hamer to the side to smash the pieces apart to open the path.

Finally, hit the button in the next room to cause a series of platforms to drop, returning you back down to floor 3F. This leads back to the central area of the large western room, where you can break apart the large grey rocks to enter an area above the prison.

There's a blue block here, which you can use the Song of Time. This opens one more hole leading down to the switch you need to bash with the Megaton Hammer to free the nearby Goron.

He's got a small Treasure chest for you, and will remind you about that large statue at the entry hall to the temple.

With the last small key in your possession, it's time to return back to where it all began. As it happens there's a giant panel right by where the Goron was imprisoned, that connects to the pillar where you last saw Darunia. Hit it with your Megaton Hammer, and you'll drop all the way back down to floor 1F putting you in front of the Boss Door.

Return to the entry room, and smash apart the large statue to reveal a locked door that you can use your last small key on. You can keep your hammer out, and put it to use smashing all the Lava Slugs in the next room until the far door unlocks. The hammer will even send the slugs into the air and douse them immediately with its shockwave!

In the room beyond, you'll be in another close quarters scenario, forcing you to block incoming Flying Tiles as a Like Like slowly stalks toward you from across the room. Keep your distance until the tiles are gone, and then use your Hookshot to stun and stab the monster, or if you really want to play it safe, send some Bombs/Bombchus toward it.

In the same room with the Flying Tiles and Like Like (much like the first) there's another Gold Skulltula hiding here as well. This one is more hidden, and to reach it you'll need to break apart the large grey rock at the end of the room with your Megaton Hammer.

Hammer apart the large statue blocking the next door, and you'll have a rematch with the Flare Dancer. This time, you can try out the Megaton Hammer to slam down after Hookshoting its metal body out, and it will stun the foe and knock it down letting you get some free hits in.

However, as it takes more damage, it will regenerate while sending green flames out. There's much more of these than when you had to dodge blue flames, so move carefully and don't get greedy chasing down the Flare Dancer.

When this second dancer goes down, you'll unlock passage to the south, as well as a small Treasure Chest that holds a Red Rupee!

In the next room, you'll finally find the last Goron Prisoner -- the one you've spotted at the very beginning cowering next to an ornate, blue treasure chest.

He has been keeping a massive blue Treasure Chest safe for you, containing the Boss Key!

Now it's finally time to help out Darunia. Return to the entry hall and go east to cross the pillar you knocked down. While you're here, be sure to Hookshot over to the north side. There's a high ledge to climb up here with several pots to restore health and magic, as well as a Fairy you should probably bottle!

When you're ready, use your Boss Key to enter the Dragon's Lair...

The Subterranean Lava Dragon, Volvagia is the terror of Death Mountain, and can emit giant blasts of fire from its mouth as it flies across its deadly lair.

Perhaps not the same type of dragon you might have been expecting, Volvagia is tremendous but also lithe, with a long body made for burrowing through the lava itself. In fact, it will spend much of this encounter trying to ambush you from the many lava holes built into its lair.

When the battle starts, it will emerge from one of these nearby lava pools, whipping its fiery mane around, and then emitting a blast of fire from its maw.

As soon as you see an opening, race forward and make a jumping leap attack with your new Megaton Hammer. You'll be able to smash apart the helm Volvagia wears, stunning it and allowing to strike at the crack on the dragon's forehead.

After your initial assuaut, Volvagia will retreat, and then emerge from the pools to float around the arena. Don't get comfortable, and prepare to take evasive actions.

At this point, Volvagia will emit a beam of fiery breath as it glides across the arena leaving a trail of fire in its wake. Always dash perpendicular to its attack route to avoid the flames! These fire trails will leave lasting smouldering spots along the arena, so take care to avoid them as Volvagia returns to the lava tunnels to make its next ambush. At this point, it will try and fake you out by causing several lava opening to bubble up.

Don't fall for the first few rumblings, but keep yourself close to the next couple so you can close the distance fast. If you take too long to get over to Volvagia next appearance, you'll end up taking a facefull of fire before you can ready your Megaton Hammer.

When you get your next hit off on its skull and slash away, Volvagia will try a new approach when taking to the air. This time, the dragon will shake the ceiling of the arena, causing burning meteors to rain down all around.

Even if you can't target the dragon, hold ZL to shield up, and strafe to the side and backwards. Try to angle yourself so that any boulders will hit you on the front where you can deflect -- if they hit you near the back your shield can't block them.

Keep up the routine of playing wack-a-mole with Volvagia's face when the dragon dares show itself another time, so long as you can close the distance fast enough. Volvagia will try for even more fake-outs, causing more and more pools to bubble up at once to keep you guessing, so try to orient yourself near the groups as much as possible.

In its final aerial assault, it will opt to blanket part of the arena in a fiery trail not once but twice, so be ready to keep moving and watch the smoldering spots. If you're quick, you can even get off a shot or two from your bow as Volvagia prepares for its fly-by.

With one more wack to the head, you should be able to deliver the killing blow to the dragon with another set of sword slash follow-ups. When its reign of terror finally comes to an end, you'll find a new Heart Container as a reward!

Enter the blue light, and you'll be taken back to the Chamber of Sages. As you might have guessed, the new Sage of Fire is your Sworn Brother, Darunia! While he will no longer able to lead the Goron people or be there for his son, Darunia is committed to taking the fight to Ganondorf, and will add his resolve to yours by giving Link the Fire Medallion.

At last, peace returns to Death Mountain, and the Gorons are safe once more. There's still much of Hyrule that needs saving, but you can at least take a moment to celebrate with all the Gorons and test out your new Megaton Hammer in a few ways:

Back in the Death Mountain Crater, there's a large grey rock off to the right side when exiting Goron City. Bashing it apart will reveal a Grotto below, where two Lizalfos guard a Treasure Chest with a Purple Rupee.

You can also clear the way to the top of the summit through the crater by bashing apart more large grey rocks along a walkway to the south. Just to the side of the broken bridge you can clear away, another grey rock is hiding something bigger - the entrance to a new Great Fairy Fountain Inside, you'll once again need to announce yourself with Zelda's Lullaby. Detecting you've met some of the other Great Fairies, this one will up the cost of her blessing, and require 200 Rupees!

Pay the offering price, and the Great Fairy of Wisdom will appear before you. Her gift is a pretty important one: The Gift of Doubled Magic! With it, your magic meter is increased, letting you use a lot more Din's Fire, and you'll soon be finding other ways to use up that magic meter of yours, too...

Heading outside onto the summit, you'll encounter someone who wasn't here before: Biggoron. The giant blacksmith is almost as big as all of Death Mountain. He apparently makes some really great weapons, but right now he's not taking any orders, so you'll have to come back when the time is right.

Be sure to hop down from Death Mountain Summit, down the mesh wall and down the slope leading back to trail to Goron City. There's a large grey rock here that wasn't before, and now that you have the Megaton Hammer, you can smash it apart. If night has fallen, you'll find a Gold Skulltula hiding behind it!

While its still nighttime, head back down the slope dodging the rolling boulders until you reach the large tunnel leading to Goron City. Look for a spot just to the left of a balcony overlooking Dodongo Cavern that once held a Bomb Flower. Next to it is a large grey rock, and if you smash it during the night, a Gold Skulltula can be found on the other side!

For a final small reward, head back into Goron City, and return to the large chamber full of rocks in the northwest on the top floor. You still can't break open the large black stones, but the grey ones can be broken up to reveal a path to one more small Treasure Chest holding a Red Rupee!

With everything completed in the Death Mountain region and the Fire Medallion obtained, it's time to track down the next Sage location. Sheik's words mentioned a temple under a vast lake, but Lake Hylia appears to have dried up. Sounds like there's a Disaster in Zora Domain worth investigating next.
